newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Warehouse blames politics for slow sales.
newsitem.headline: Warehouse blames politics for slow sales.

text.p: Warehouse Group Ltd Managing Director Stephen Tindall said on Wednesday political uncertainty and bad weather were having an impact on sales.

Tindall, asked what he thought the reason was for indifferent sales over November and the first quarter, said: "Probably because we have not got a government at the moment. There is obviously uncertainty out there in the market place.
"Secondly I think the season started off from an inclement weather point of view and that does have a big effect early in the season on us," Tindall said after the annual meeting.
Long, hot periods meant more sales of summer furniture and apparel.
Tindall earlier told the meeting that sales in the first quarter and in November had been erratic, but that he was confident the quarter ending in January would be on track.
He said the next five weeks would be "difficult for everyone" but that sales were not far off track at present.
"There is no steady pattern to them and I think that's because of the election."

Asked about the possible long term effects of shopping services provided on the Internet, Tindall said there were undoubtedly products that lent themselves to the network, particularly wine, music and videos. Studies had shown weekly grocery shopping on the Internet was also quite successful.

"But I think shopping is still New Zealanders' favourite passtime, quite clearly by the surveys that have been done," Tindall said. By 12.35 p.m. (2335 GMT) shares in the Warehouse were trading at NZ$3.24, down six cents.
